sentences.text: How are you?
I'm good, thank you.
How are you doing?
This meeting is being recorded.
Traveling today, so I am on the go, but all is good.
How are you?
Yeah, busy, busy for an Easter Monday to jump off another client call.
We're in the middle of making an offer to an agent acquire.
But yeah, I got one more call after this and then and I'll enjoy a bit of Jesus time, celebrate, you know.
Yeah.
What about you traveling today?
So I am in San Diego.
My flight yesterday was ended up being cancelled so I'm just at a hotel now waiting for our flight to take off which is going to be later in the day.
So just getting some work done at the hotel.
But yeah, so just yeah, staying busy.
But I, you know, been following along with what you guys are doing and seems pretty, pretty complementary to what we're doing as well.
You know, it sounds like yours is.
You've got a few different things going on.
Yeah.
But you know, I thought it would be good for you and I to kind of connect and kind of share some notes and see if there's an opportunity to maybe partner up in some way.
Yeah, definitely.
Could be interesting.
So yeah, there's a couple of things in there.
Firstly, you've signed an NDA for one of our clients on the sell side on Agencies Co.
Yeah, yeah.
So yeah, I mean just initial discussions about that.
So I know we did talk and you've done multiple acquisitions before so.

Right, yeah, you guys are obviously in motion but we always like to have a quick call before, before we, we put our client in, in touch just kind of to see where the buyer actually is and whether it's a, a transaction of the size that they can do that sort of thing.
So yeah, I mean that, that's just like the initial, the initial conversation is, you know, is this the right size for you guys?
It's, it's quite a big acquisition and I know you guys have, have done maybe the same size or a little bit smaller, but.
Yeah, that's right.
Yeah.

So tell me before we jump into this particular deal, I'd love to because I know you are obviously operating kind of an investment banker capacity or broker capacity and then you also are kind of executing on a roll up yourself, is that right?
So can you kind of just give me a quick background of kind of your, what you're up to as well and then we can dive into the specific target as well.
Yeah, so, so we are doing a roll up.

So basically we, we've, we've been working on roll ups for Clients for, for a long time and more, more so more often we, that we've actually been working on the sell side for what are called virtual roll ups.
So essentially you're taking a disparate group of agencies or businesses and you find a bunch of these buyers that all want to exit.
But by putting them together into a group and then exiting them together, you get a better multiple for everybody that's in the group.
We've been working on the sell side of these for investment banks and investors and investment groups and also fast growth agencies that have done a couple of these.
And are you doing them simply through, let's say you're taking five agencies at a million of ebitda, putting them together.
There's no cash exchange but it's purely kind of a agreement on governance and ownership of that holding co and then doing some kind of light integration.
Yeah, that's exactly it.
So the opportunity really is for those agency owners to skip a step rather than get absorbed into a financial buyer and missing the arbitrage opportunity or taking a small cut of it.

What we're doing is we're turning that over to the founders so they can pretty much, I mean it might not be exact but we're looking to sort of get close to doubling because we know most of these agencies are worth between four and six on their own.
So five say but as part of a larger exit they could be part of an 8 to 12 times multiple.
So the time to get around, you know, between 5 and 8 million EBITDA because the economics really start to change around there.
Yeah, like these double digits.
So, so we will put the businesses together.
Like you said, it's going to be some light integration.
So we'll have our, our operations guy working to see where this, the sort of low hanging fruit is and what we want to do.
Create a story and you know, get it right for the acquirer.
So usually it is most likely private equity who, who pay better multiples anyway.
But also they like the, this type of work.
It's what they do.
You know, they can get their clipboards and their pens out and start making cost savings on the back end.
But for sure all of these businesses are ready and exiting at these double digit multiples or close to versus just exiting on their own.
So that, that multiple is what we're giving the founders a share.
Really the big difference because financial acquirers, they won't do that.
And so it's only this sort of unique model that allows agency owners to, to exit in this way unless it yourself of course.
Which is kind of what you're in the process of as well.
So, and so you're doing kind of like, like with each of these kind of roll ups, each of them kind of have a thesis where you're saying, okay, we're going to do a focus on performance marketing.
The one's going to be maybe you know, geared towards a specific industry or is it kind of more agnostic in that sense where, you know, just kind of based on the, the economics.
It makes sense.
No, definitely not agnostic.
Yeah.
What we're looking to do is, is leverage our experience in the space.
I mean this is another thing that's a big difference with financial buyers.
They will just lump five disparate agencies into a group.
Right.
They'll do the integration, but they don't really share clients or work.
Yeah.
So what we're looking to do is, is find companies that do really work together.
So either they would have some horizontal shared expertise or they work in the same vertical and are able to share clients, similar clients thing.
So for instance, we have an E commerce one that we've got a couple in already.
They've got a really good overlap.
One's sort of more an expertise in E commerce generally.
The other is an Amazon partner.
And so they're not really cannibalizing each other's businesses, but they have some shared expertise that we can help them to model where they could integrate in future.
And then it makes much better sense to a buyer that just sees this as an E commerce play and is able to just dive in, take the whole thing and get the integration done themselves.
So yeah, yeah, so we'll look at, we'll look at two different things.
Vertical, like I say vertical, horizontal.
Okay.
Merges.
Yeah.
Yep.
Yeah, no, that's, that's great.
And so your role in that really is to kind of come in, you know, obviously find the, you know, thank you.
You know, find the right agencies, put them together.
You guys are kind of identifying, you know, the synergies.
You know, how long are you guys kind of putting them together before you guys go back to market?
So we kind of envisaged it taken about six months to, to, to find each group.
I mean we, this is what we do.
So we, we kind of know what we do.
We're experts in the field.
We talk to hundreds of agencies every month.
Somebody in my team is, you know, we're always meeting new sellers and buyers.
So yeah, so yeah, it shouldn't take too long around a six month period to get the group together and Then it probably will take about the same period to get it sold.
So usually takes three or four months to get a buyer.

I mean we will do some of this in tandem because we're already speaking some private equity firms, but just to be conservative about it would usually take about six months to get the, the deal done as well.
And.
Okay.
Yeah, so we're looking at something like a 12 month window to get the deal out the door.
Okay, that's helpful.
Okay, well no, that's, that all sounds good.
And then the, the deals that you have on market have though they just want to kind of sell independently versus kind of going the, the roll up route.
I assume so, yeah.

So I mean we, we may look at this depending on how, how close we are to getting the deal over the line, but we, we really need to have 1 million plus EBITDA agencies for it to work easy and fair across, across the, the groupings.
So yeah, I mean we have an independent company.
Some of them are just ready to exit.
They don't want the faff of, of you know, having to do an integration.
They're ready to go.
Others are just too small and we wouldn't, we wouldn't even put them into the group.
So yeah, those are the ones that you see listed.
Got it.
Okay.
No, that's super helpful man.
I appreciate you giving me the background.
I mean, you know, we're.
And you come from an agency background, is that right?
Yeah, I actually exited my own business nine years ago.
Okay.
And then kind of accidentally went into M A.
Yeah.
But basically my, I had a friend who was CEO of a listed company and he wanted to acquire businesses like the one that I'd sold.
So.
Okay.
Him and his investor who was sort of old school agency guy in his 70s who'd already done a huge roll up and exited.
He took me under his wife, trained me up.
Yeah.
And.
Oh, that's awesome.
Then went into it that way from an agency side.
So.
It'S awesome man.
That's, I mean it's a fun space to be in, you know, especially you know, having both the, the knowledge and kind of the marketing agency and services space and you know, combining that with M and A.
Because obviously it's a very fragmented space.
There's a lot of opportunities to, to execute on something like this.
So that's, that's great.

Okay, so, so tell me so I can tell you a little bit about what we're doing just so you, you kind of have an understanding and then I'd love to, you know, obviously better Understand the target that I reached out about and, you know, also just kind of get your feedback on, you know, what do you think is, you know, a potential, you know, path forward here?

Because I think right now I'm, you know, pretty opportunistic for looking at, you know, deals that, you know, for us we've probably, probably got a maybe a two year time horizon before we turn around and exit.
And so, you know, again, just kind of open to different ways of looking at this.
But in 2022, we started to change from kind of growing organically to M and A, which as you know, is a totally different strategy.
And so we raised some debt and equity in 2022 basically to execute on tucking acquisitions, which, yeah, to your point, we've done four deals so far.
All of them, except for one, was somewhat equal in size to us at the time.
I would say, you know, sub 1 million of EBITDA, you know, typically ranging anywhere from a million to 10 million in revenue.

We have one deal right now that we are pretty much at the purchase agreement that will, in theory, kind of double the business from this transaction, which will put us at about, let's call it 15 million of net revenue, about 35 million in gross.
And then I'd say about three to three and a half million of EBITDA is kind of where, no, we'll end up after this next transaction.
And so, you know, for us, I mean, to your point, which has been kind of our north star in doing this, is, you know, getting north of 5 million of EBITDA before we turn around and exit.
So that's kind of our, I'd say, entry point to starting to, you know, go to market and think that there's interesting parties to acquire the business.
And I would say, you know, we're hoping to get there, like I said, in the next one to two years.
And so, you know, we've started out as a social media agency that's kind of been at the core of what we do.
So our thesis is, you know, socially led marketing.
Our model is a fully kind of retainer recurring revenue model.
I'd say probably 98% of our revenue is just all annual recurring revenue.
We have a productized service that has kind of different tiers and kind of menu of services versus everything's, you know, fully custom.
And, you know, our integration strategy has been less on kind of a holding toe and more of a branded house where, you know, we're doing a full integration of the companies when they come in.
Obviously, given the size of each deal Sometimes that can happen within, you know, as little as 60 days.
And sometimes, like our biggest one that we did to date in 2023 took about a year, you know, to fully integrate.
But that's been kind of a part of our strategy, so.
Yeah.
And I definitely be really curious to kind of learn a bit more about this target specifically.
It did seem like there was, you know, some synergies just kind of outside looking in.
And so I thought it, again, be worthwhile to reach out to you and kind of better understand this target specifically and if it fits into our, you know, kind of our mandate.
Yeah, it looks good.
I think it does look like a good fit.
Their focus isn't social media.
They are.
They're buying media mostly.
So whether that's it, I don't know.
But they're working a lot in the entertainment space, and they've got some business in education as well and technology.
So it's.
It's quite a fun business as well.
Based in New York, and I think they're knocking on the door now.
1.5 million EBITDA, although we've got them listed a little bit.
A little bit lower, but they're.
They're certainly growing and going in the right direction.
So they could fit nice into your timeline, given the size.
Yeah.
Put you right to the doors on 5 million EBITDA, which would be good.
Yep.
Absolutely.
Could definitely be a fit.
And then, so you guys are, what, you're raising, uh, debt, uh, against each acquisition.
Yeah.
And kind of the full parent company.
So, yeah, we're looking at kind of deal by deal.
Our capital partners have kind of looked at these deal by deal, and they've been obviously supportive of the strategy and continue to deploy capital in these deals.
I'd say all the deals so far have been off market, so this would kind of be one that, you know, I'd consider on market, but it's no, you know, there's no issues there at all with that.
But just so you know, most of our outreach has been proprietary and, you know, kind of looking at these deal by deal, and we structure, you know, each deal, you know, a bit differently.
So, you know, I know there's a lot of financial buyers that have a very kind of regimented approach to how they structure these deals.

Ours is a bit more really from a strategic acquired lens, you know, so we'll look at, you know, is there some synergies here where we can identify revenue synergies, potential costs, redundancies, things like that?
So.
Yeah.
So why are they looking to sell I know they've been, from what I saw, been around for a while, right.
Yeah.
So to be honest with you, they're not.
Then.
They're not desperate to sell at all.
What happened was we.
We were.
These guys have been a client on the buy side and acquired a business last year.
Okay.
And then we were approached to see if they wanted to sell by quite a large agency.
And so we decided if.
If there was interest out there, that it might be a better approach for them to.
To actually just list and go.
Go to market and see if there was more than.
Than just the one.
So, yeah, there was no real, real rush to get to it.
We actually instigated it.
But they are, you know, they're interested in exploring.
I mean, they have been doing a long time, and so I think given that they've had interest immediately, yeah, they're now exploring what the options might look like.
So, I mean, we haven't got any offers yet.
We've only been in the market for a few weeks, so very, very early.
And I think they would be.
To speak with you, Alex, because you have a strategy to exit again, which I think they would be interested in.
Yeah.
Because.
Yeah, that was going to be my.
My question is kind of the appetite for, you know, second bite of the apple pretty shortly thereafter.

You know, obviously with the multiple that, you know, you and I are both on the same page, I think we can unlock, you know, double digits multiple, you know, assuming everything checks out just given our stickiness and retention and a lot of the other things that, aside from just ebitda, you know, expansion, but that's good to know.
And how many partners are there?
I believe there's just one.
There might be some.
Okay.
Just small percentages, but it's, it's mostly Brooke who owns and operates the business, so.
Okay, very good.
Okay.
Yeah, well, I definitely think we'd be, you know, wanting to.
To take a look at this, so if you.
I know that the next step.
I think you guys sent over that sim, so I thought the deck was really helpful if they do have a data room that I can start, you know, kind of sharing internally.
You know, ideally, you know, I can just kind of speak from the appetite of our, you know, capital partners.
They would love to do kind of a subsequent transaction because we're kind of all thinking along the lines of, okay, how do we kind of pretty quickly get, you know, past that 5 million of EBITDA?
And so if we can, you know, kind of get this next deal done, which we've already, you know, it's already in the bag.
It's, you know, we anticipate closing either end of this month or start of May, and then we're looking to kind of execute on a, on a follow on deal.
And so, you know, I think it's something we can move pretty quickly on.
So.
Yeah, I would love to see the data room, any other materials that you guys have.
And then I think we have a.
Process with this so on.
Okay.
Once we've got the signed, the signed NDA and you've.
We've shared the im, then we don't actually move until we've, we've set up a meeting and there's chemistry.
Okay.
We just feel like, you know, we're doing a lot of work up, up front and then one or the other side just says, yeah, no, it's not going to work.
Which we Fairly, fairly high percentages of that.
So it just helps us minimize that and also keeps the privacy of our clients.
Makes total sense.
Yeah, I'm, I'm all good with that.
So I, I would like to be.
A call basically with Brooke, see how you guys get on.

Perfect.
Yeah, I think that sounds like a great next step.

Okay, perfect.
All right, well, good to catch up again.
Yes, likewise.
Thank you, Andy.
I appreciate it, man.
Enjoy your Easter Monday.
I know it's later your time, so I appreciate it.
Yeah, you've got a whole day ahead of you.
Maybe you'll get back in time.
Yeah.
Good luck.
Appreciate it.
Cheers.
Okay, cheers.

summary.overview: The Business Development and Acquisition Opportunity Discussion meeting between Rossman Media and Capital A, led by Andy Day, focused on exploring potential acquisition strategies to enhance Rossman Media's growth trajectory. Andy introduced his company's model of "virtual roll-ups," where they combine agencies with synergistic EBITDA of $1M+ to achieve better exit multiples, targeting a total of $5-8 million EBITDA for optimal valuations. Rossman Media has pivoted from organic growth to mergers and acquisitions, having completed four deals since 2022, with a goal to double their business through a new acquisition that would elevate their EBITDA significantly. The discussion highlighted a specific target agency in the entertainment sector with $1.5M EBITDA, which aligns with Rossman's objectives. Action items included ensuring the signing of an NDA and setting up a call between Rossman and the target agency's owner, Brooke, to establish further synergy and expedite the acquisition process.
summary.short_summary: Andy Day led a discussion between Rossman Media and Capital A, centering on acquisition strategies to bolster Rossman Media's growth. He introduced the concept of 'virtual roll-ups,' which involves merging agencies with synergistic EBITDA exceeding $1M to achieve higher exit multiples, aiming for a combined EBITDA of $5-8 million for favorable valuations. Since pivoting from organic growth to mergers and acquisitions, Rossman Media has completed four deals since 2022 and is focused on a new acquisition to significantly elevate their EBITDA. A specific target agency in the entertainment sector, with an EBITDA of $1.5M, was identified as aligning with Rossman's goals. Key action items included signing an NDA and arranging a call with the target agency's owner, Brooke, to foster synergy and expedite the acquisition process.
